notes: ACCESS: tier (a) direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi impersonate=chrome) worked for all pages; robots.txt explicitly Allows ClaudeBot and User-agent:* (only /_svc/ and /_vs/ disallowed, which were never used). Playwright (tier b) was tried first for count verification but every navigation failed with net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR / timeout (protocol-level anti-bot fingerprinting of plain headless Chromium), so tier (b) was abandoned per the first-block rule. Tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome was used only to verify, in a real hydrated browser, that the SSR count matches the fully-rendered UI count (it does, exactly) before relying on the HTTP-only method for the rest of the extraction. TREE: noon.com embeds its full category taxonomy (id_category/code/name/children) as a React Server Components data blob in each category page (search for code:"category" -> data:$R[n]=[...]). This blob was parsed (bracket-matched and converted to JSON) for the Storage & Organisation, Bedding, Bath, Home Decor and Patio/Lawn/Garden top-level pages to enumerate every sub/leaf category and its exact slug; the top mega-menu (embedded on the homepage) was used to identify which top-level sections to expand. Every leaf URL used was confirmed valid (200, correct breadcrumb/H1 matching the requested node). QTY: noon.com does not expose an exact per-category product count through any accessible tier. Every category page renders a search-style header ("N Results for <Category> in UAE") where the displayed count is rounded/abbreviated (e.g. "100K+", "30K+", "900+") for any count above roughly one thousand, and the underlying nbHits integer itself is a broad text-relevance match count (matching the category display name as a free-text query across the whole catalog) rather than a verified category-membership total -- confirmed by an implausibly large (over 1 million) count appearing for ordinary categories, and reproduced identically in a fully hydrated real Chrome tab (tier c), so this is not merely an SSR-only artifact. Only leaf pages whose displayed count is the literal un-rounded integer (matching the internal nbHits value exactly, e.g. "1", "46", "72", "5") were treated as exact and given a numeric qty; every other row (the large majority) is qty=null with a "MANUAL REVIEW" flag explaining the rounding. No count was ever estimated, rounded, or inferred. EXCLUDED: Lighting (all Decor Lighting / Bathroom Lighting / Garden and Patio Lighting nodes), Furniture (Wardrobes, Dressers, Storage Cabinets, Storage Benches and Shoe Racks explicitly placed under the site's Furniture taxonomy branch, per storage.md #21/#27 "if the website explicitly places the product inside a Furniture category, prefer Furniture"), Kitchen & Dining serveware/cookware/appliances, bathroom fixtures and hardware (showerheads, towel bars/hooks/rings, taps, toilets, sinks), purely decorative Home Decor Accents (vases, candles, frames, ornaments, sculptures, wall art/wallpaper, mirrors, clocks, home fragrance), Trash and Recycling (waste-disposal containers do not fit the Storage rule set's scope), Artificial Flora, apparel and footwear (Bath Slippers), medical/orthopedic pillow variants (Cervical, Lumbar, Leg Positioner, Specialty Medical, Bed Wedge and Reading pillows), and inflatable beds/pillows (non-textile air/vinyl camping-style products). A few genuinely ambiguous leaves were kept at LOW confidence rather than dropped (Blinds & Shades mixes textile and non-textile materials; Rug Pads, Cookie Jars, Compost, Utensil Holders and Umbrella Racks are borderline per the respective rule files' own examples) -- see each row's flag/confidence.
